text:
Ava K: heads-up — seeing repeated GPU queue spikes in us-west2 over the last 6 hrs, tail latencies for large-chat jobs hitting 4-6s, cost also up. Suspect noisy tenants driving continuous micro-bursts.
Rory M: saw that dash — queue depth up to 120 per node for a few minutes then drops. Any specific tenant IDs?
Ava K: yes, tenant-124 and tenant-88 show most of the bursts, heavy sampling of long-context generations. Logs: `gpu_queue_length=118 node=gpu-73 tenant=tenant-124 seq_len=2048`.
Jamal S: sounds like classic noisy-neighbor. Current per-tenant soft limits? we only do static rate limits per API key right now.
Priya N: we have admission control at LB layer but it doesn't account for backend queue or KV cache pressure. So clients can swamp kernels while the queue backs up.
Ava K: proposal: add a token-bucket per-tenant enforced at the cluster ingress that tracks "compute tokens" (weighted by model and sequence length). When bucket empties, either queue with backpressure or reject fast with 429. Also add soft-eviction on nodes when tenant exceeds memory pressure for KV caches.
Rory M: +1 on weighted tokens. Implementation idea: tokens consumed = ceil(tokens_per_request * seq_len / 512). tokens_per_request derived from model profile. That way long contexts pay more.
Jamal S: we should simulate before rollout. Also need fairness for shared-pool tenants vs reserved tenants. Reserved should be prioritized, fallback to low-cost variants if no capacity.
Priya N: question: eviction is risky — evicting KV cache for a tenant can harm latency drastically after eviction. Can we do graceful TTL-based shrink + replicate caches to hot-tier SSD before evict?
Ava K: yep — soft-eviction flow: when node memory pressure > 85% triggered by a tenant, mark tenant as "degraded" on that node, reduce their token refill rate by 50% and signal orchestrator to migrate long-lived sessions out during next maintenance window. If immediate free required, evict only cold KV segments first.
Rory M: sounds good. What about metrics / SLOs we need to expose so product can track impact?
Priya N: add per-tenant: token_consumed_total, token_rejects_429, avg_queue_wait_ms, kv_eviction_count, node_mem_pressure_percent. Dashboards + alerts when token_reject_rate > 1% for >5m.
Jamal S: cost angle — token buckets give predictable quota usage so we can convert to committed capacity pricing for Dedicated customers. Also reduces burst-related autoscale churn.
Ava K: I'll sketch an RFC. Quick implementation sketch:

```
# ingress filter (pseudo)
on request(req):
  tokens = compute_tokens(req.model, req.seq_len)
  if token_bucket[tenant].take(tokens):
    forward(req)
  else:
    if tenant.is_reserved: queue_hint(req) else return 429
```

Rory M: for simulation we can replay last 48h trace to a local cluster with token-bucket tuning grid. I can own that.
Priya N: I'll prototype the KV soft-eviction heuristics (cold segment detection + SSD spill) and run microbenchmarks.
Jamal S: infra-bot: create ticket and link RFC when ready.
infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-1427: "Tenant token-buckets + KV soft-eviction RFC" (assignee: Ava K).
Ava K: timeline suggestion: simulate + prototype over next 2 weeks, RFC end of sprint, canary in us-west2 only, then eu-west1. Rollback plan: disable token enforcement (fast path) and restore kv caches from snapshots.
Rory M: can we avoid surprising customers? need email/SLAs for reserved tenants when they get degraded. Add a soft-warning header in API responses when tenant token usage > 80%.
Priya N: +1 to warning header: `X-Redwood-Token-Usage: 82%` and `Retry-After` when 429s.
Ava K: OK let's proceed. Action items: Rory -> simulation (due in 5 days), Priya -> KV prototype (7 days), Jamal -> draft pricing/SLAs impact note (7 days). I'll write RFC skeleton today.
Jamal S: thanks all. one more perf note: include node-level admission score = f(queue_depth, kernel_util, mem_pressure) so token decisions can be routed to less-loaded nodes rather than blunt reject.
Ava K: good catch — include routing hint in RFC. End of thread.
